conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: You’re talking about an umbrella, right?
Respondent: Yes, that’s right.
Respondent: Whether he goes to school or out to play, as long as he leaves the house, he always holds an umbrella.
Respondent: He started doing this after my wife passed away.
Respondent: When my wife was still in the hospital bed, she said some things to Minghao.
Respondent: She made an agreement with Minghao. She said that mom would go to heaven first to protect you.
Respondent: At that time, Minghao sat far away and didn’t say a word, but I remember he let out a soft sigh.
Respondent: I think he might have wanted to tell his mom that there is no such thing as heaven in this world, and that mom should stay by our side to protect us.
Respondent: But he didn’t say it out loud.
Respondent: After my wife passed away, it was only after a long time that I noticed Minghao always held an umbrella whenever he went out.
Respondent: Only then did I remember what exactly the agreement between my wife and Minghao was.
Respondent: Mom didn’t lie to you, okay? From now on, when it rains, mom can’t come to pick you up...
Respondent: If one day it rains and you forget to bring an umbrella, I will make the rain stop, okay?
